items.front: Part III range and how many Fundamental Rights now?
items.back: Articles 12-35; six FRs now (originally seven). Right to Property was the dropped seventh.
items.examPoint: Part III & scope — Articles 12-35, borrowed from US Bill of Rights / UDHR

items.front: Under which Fundamental Right does abolition of untouchability (Art 17) fall?
Present status of the Right to Property?
items.back: A legal/constitutional right under Article 300A (available to any person); ceased to be a FR by the 44th Amendment 1978.
items.examPoint: Six Fundamental Rights now (originally 7); Right to Property removed by 44th Amendment 1978 → Article 300A legal right

items.front: Right to Privacy — which Article and which case?
items.back: Article 21 (life & personal liberty); K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017), 9-judge bench.
items.examPoint: Article 21 — life & personal liberty; Maneka Gandhi expansion

items.front: Right to marry a person of one's choice is protected under which Article?
items.back: Article 21 (part of the right to life and personal liberty).
items.examPoint: Article 21 — life & personal liberty; Maneka Gandhi expansion

items.front: What exactly does the Right against Exploitation (Art 23-24) cover?
items.back: Art 23: traffic in humans, begar & forced labour; Art 24: no child below 14 in factory/mine/hazardous work.
items.examPoint: Articles 23-24 — right against exploitation (trafficking, forced labour, child labour)

items.front: Why did Ambedkar call Article 32 the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?
items.back: It lets a person move the Supreme Court directly to enforce Fundamental Rights via five writs.
items.examPoint: Article 32 — right to constitutional remedies ('heart and soul', Ambedkar)

items.back: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, Quo Warranto.
items.examPoint: Writs — Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, Quo Warranto

items.front: Whose writ jurisdiction is wider — SC (Art 32) or HC (Art 226)?
items.back: High Court (Art 226) — it covers FRs AND any other legal right; Art 32 is only for FRs.
items.examPoint: Writs — Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, Quo Warranto

items.front: Which FRs can NEVER be suspended, even during a National Emergency?
items.back: Articles 20 and 21 (made non-suspendable by the 44th Amendment 1978). Art 358 auto-suspends Art 19.
items.examPoint: Emergency suspension (Art 358/359; 44th Amdt shields Arts 20 & 21); citizens vs all persons

items.front: Is the right to vote and to be elected a Fundamental Right?
items.back: No — it is a constitutional/legal right (not a FR), conferred by the Constitution and RPA laws.
items.examPoint: Right to vote and be elected — a constitutional/legal right, not a Fundamental Right

items.front: Article 14 combines which two ideas, and from where?
items.back: Equality before law (British) + equal protection of laws (American). Rule of law bars arbitrary/unguided discretion.
items.examPoint: Article 14 — equality before law & equal protection of laws; Rule of Law (Dicey) features

items.front: Besides FRs, which parts of the Constitution reflect the UDHR 1948?
items.examPoint: Part III & scope — Articles 12-35, borrowed from US Bill of Rights / UDHR

items.front: Which FRs are for citizens only vs all persons?
items.back: Citizens only: Arts 15, 16, 19, 29, 30. All persons (incl. foreigners): Arts 14, 20, 21, 21A, 22, 25-28.
items.examPoint: Article 19 — six freedoms and reasonable restrictions
